title: Jaga Durian
subject: three cousins on the night shift in a durian orchard hut in Kuala Pilah, racing each other in the dark to every thud
caption: Negeri Sembilan caklempong folk song in the Minangkabau gong-chime tradition. Rows of small bossed kettle-gongs, the handheld caklempong pacik and the rack-mounted caklempong duduk, playing bright interlocking melodic patterns; a double-headed gendang driving a quick dance rhythm; a low hanging gong struck at the end of each phrase; a bansi bamboo flute answering the vocal lines. Open-air and lively, the gong-chimes forward and ringing, the gendang punchy, voices dry. A bright male folk lead singing short lines with a grin in his voice, the ensemble shouting the written sorak replies. 128 BPM, G major. Rowdy, proud and half asleep. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no rock band, no synths, no accordion, no joget violin or 6/8 lilt, no dangdut beat, no autotune.
lyrics:
[Intro - caklempong interlocking pattern and gendang]

[Verse 1]
Musim durian, Kuala Pilah, malam Sabtu
Pondok buluh, lampu suluh, ubat nyamuk dua gelung
Den dengan Pian, dengan Adik Kecik
Tiga sepupu, satu termos kopi o

[Pre-Chorus]
Angin bertiup, dahan bergoyang
Semua diam, telinga panjang

[Chorus]
Gedebuk! Siapa dulu?
(Den dulu! Den dulu!)
Lari dalam gelap, tersadung akar
Durian jatuh, tiga orang jatuh

[Verse 2]
Pukul dua, Pian dah berdengkur
Adik Kecik lari, balik bawa kelapa
Pukul tiga, bunyi kuat kat belakang
Ekau tahu siapa? Pian, tergolek dari pondok

[Chorus]
Gedebuk! Siapa dulu?
(Den dulu! Den dulu!)
Subuh nanti kira, tiga puluh dua biji
Satu kelapa, satu Pian, semua masuk bakul

[Outro - caklempong and sorak, one low gong]
Musim depan, den jaga sorang!
(Hoi! Hoi!)
